facts.statement: Thalattoarchon was described in 2013 based on a single partial skeleton found in Nevada.
facts.quote: The taxon was described in 2013 from a single partial skeleton discovered in Nevada.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon was a large predatory ichthyosaur that lived in North America during the Middle Triassic period.
facts.quote: Thalattoarchon is a genus of large, Middle Triassic predatory ichthyosaurs from North America

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Thalattoarchon was discovered in 1997 by paleontologist Jim Holstein in the Augusta Mountains of Nevada.
facts.quote: The only specimen of Thalattoarchon was discovered in 1997 by the paleontologist Jim Holstein during a field expedition in the Augusta Mountains, located in Nevada, United States.

facts.statement: The fossils were completely exhumed in 2008 with support from the National Geographic Society after three weeks of work.
facts.quote: It was with the support and a grant from the National Geographic Society that the fossils were completely exhumed in 2008, after a period of work of three weeks.

facts.statement: The fossils date to approximately 244.6 million years ago, corresponding to the beginning of the late Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic.
facts.quote: The fossils were excavated in the Taylori Zone of the Fossil Hill Member in the Favret Formation, dating to approximately 244.6 million years ago, from the beginning of the late Anisian of the Middle Triassic.

facts.statement: In 2013, the specimen was designated the holotype for the new species Thalattoarchon saurophagis by a team including Nadia B. Fröbisch and Olivier Rieppel.
facts.quote: It was in 2013 that this specimen was designated as the holotype of a new genus and species of ichthyosaurs by Nadia B. Fröbisch, Jörg Fröbisch, P. Martin Sander, Lars Schmitz and Olivier Rieppel, under the name of Thalattoarchon saurophagis in the scientific journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon possessed large teeth with two cutting edges that could reach up to 12 cm in length.
facts.quote: The jaws of Thalattoarchon feature large teeth with two cutting edges of up to 12 cm.

facts.statement: Despite incomplete fossils, the animal is estimated to have had at least 60 presacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: Although the fossils are incomplete, the animal would have had a skeleton comprising at least 60 presacral vertebrae.

facts.statement: The original describing team estimated Thalattoarchon to be over 8.6 meters long, making it a particularly large ichthyosaur.
facts.quote: The describing team estimated the size of Thalattoarchon at over 8.6 m long, making it a particularly large ichthyosaur.

facts.statement: In 2021, researchers proposed that Thalattoarchon could have reached a body mass of 4.3 metric tons.
facts.quote: In 2021, Paul Martin Sander and colleagues proposed that the animal would reach a body mass of 4.3 MT.

facts.statement: A 2023 book by Darren Naish revised the estimated length of Thalattoarchon to 9 meters.
facts.quote: In a 2023 book, Darren Naish slightly increased the estimated length of the animal, bringing it to 9 m.

facts.statement: Unlike later ichthyosaurs which had two caudal lobes, Thalattoarchon had a long, poorly developed caudal fin.
facts.quote: Unlike the more derived (advanced-diverging) representatives dating from the Jurassic and Cretaceous, it has a long, poorly developed caudal fin, unlike the two caudal lobes present in later ichthyosaurs.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon had a remarkably large head relative to its body, a trait rarely seen in ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: The animal's head is remarkably large in proportion to its body, a trait rarely observed in representatives of the group.

facts.statement: The skull of Thalattoarchon is estimated to be 1.2 meters long.
facts.quote: The size of the skull is estimated at 1.2 m long.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon had elongated eye sockets reaching up to 29 cm, each containing a scleral ring.
facts.quote: The eye sockets are elongated, reaching up to 29 cm, and each contain a scleral ring.

facts.statement: The largest preserved tooth of Thalattoarchon is at least 12 cm long, with a crown measuring 5 cm.
facts.quote: The largest preserved tooth is at least 12 cm long, with the crown alone measuring 5 cm.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon's teeth are considered a main autapomorphy, characterized by being large, thin, having two sharp edges, and a smooth crown.
facts.quote: The teeth represent one of the main autapomorphies of Thalattoarchon, being large and thin, having two sharp edges each and a fairly smooth crown.

facts.statement: The classification of Thalattoarchon is debated, with it being placed either in the clade Merriamosauria or the basal family Cymbospondylidae.
facts.quote: The classification of this genus within the ichthyosaurs is much debated, being either classified within the clade Merriamosauria or in the more basal family Cymbospondylidae.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon is estimated to have had at least 60 vertebrae in its presacral column.
facts.quote: it is estimated that it would have had at least 60 in the presacral column.

facts.statement: The anterior dorsal vertebrae of Thalattoarchon are nearly round, measuring 10 cm in diameter and 6 cm in length.
facts.quote: The anterior dorsal vertebrae are almost round in anteroposterior view and measure 10 cm in diameter and 6 cm long.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon had a straight tail with no visible curvature or turned-down end.
facts.quote: The animal's tail appears to be rather straight, having visibly no curvature and not having a turned-down end.

facts.statement: The femur of Thalattoarchon was twice as long as the height of its caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: the length of the femur being twice the height of the caudal vertebrae.

facts.statement: In 2021, Sander and colleagues reclassified Thalattoarchon within the Merriamosauria as the sister taxon to the Shastasauridae.
facts.quote: In 2021, Sander and his colleagues reclassified Thalattoarchon within the Merriamosauria, but this time as the sister taxon of the Shastasauridae.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon lived during the Middle Triassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Triásico Medio

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon was named by Fröbisch and colleagues in 2013.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Fröbisch et al., 2013 en prensa

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon spent its entire life in the water and exhibited reduced bone ossification adapted to marine existence.
facts.quote: Ichthyosaurs like Thalattoarchon were very well-adapted to their marine existence, spending their entire lives in the water and showing reduced levels of ossification of their bones.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon was an active animal with a high metabolic rate that allowed it to maintain its body temperature.
facts.quote: Ichthyosaurs were active animals with high metabolic rates, able to maintain their body temperatures.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon is recognized as an apex predator due to its large, robust head and bicarinate cutting teeth.
facts.quote: Due to its bicarinate, cutting teeth and its large, robust head, Thalattoarchon is recognized as having been an apex predator.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon is considered the oldest known aquatic megapredator tetrapod in the fossil record.
facts.quote: All of these characteristics combined with the datatation of this taxon suggested that Thalattoarchon would have been the oldest aquatic megapredator tetrapod known in the fossil record.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Thalattoarchon hunted Cymbospondylus using a pack-hunting strategy, as this behavior is not reported in the fossil record.
facts.quote: In 2021, Sander and his colleagues suggested that if Thalattoarchon would have fed on Cymbospondylus, it would have preyed on it using a pack-hunting strategy, a behavior that is not at all reported in the fossil record.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Thalattoarchon may have fed only on smaller animals, living or dead, similar to a great white shark.
facts.quote: The authors of this study also suggest that Thalattoarchon would have only fed on smaller animals, both alive and dead, a feeding strategy comparable to that of the great white shark.

facts.statement: Due to its apex predator adaptations, Thalattoarchon likely did not feed on ammonites, squid, or fish.
facts.quote: Due to its apex predator adaptations, Thalattoarchon would not likely feed on ammonites, squid, or even fish.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon was one of the most abundant marine reptiles found in the Fossil Hill Member.
facts.quote: The most abundant marine reptiles of the Fossil Hill Member are the ichthyosaurs, including Thalattoarchon itself.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon was an extinct ichthyosaur that lived during the Middle Triassic in western United States.
facts.quote: Thalattoarchon es un género extinto de ictiosaurio que vivió durante el Triásico Medio en el oeste de Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: The type species Thalattoarchon saurophagis was discovered in Nevada in 2010 and formally described in 2013.
facts.quote: La especie tipo Thalattoarchon saurophagis (que significa "gobernante de los mares, devorador de lagartos" en griego) fue descubierta en el estado de Nevada en 2010 y fue formalmente descrita en 2013.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon is known from a single skeleton consisting of a partial skull, vertebrae, hip bones, and parts of the hind flippers.
facts.quote: Es conocido a partir de un único esqueleto consistente en un cráneo parcial, la columna vertebral, huesos de la cadera, y partes de las aletas posteriores.

facts.statement: The total length of Thalattoarchon is estimated to be at least 8.6 meters.
facts.quote: La longitud total de Thalattoarchon se estima en al menos unos 8,6 metros.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon lived four million years after the first appearance of ichthyosaurs in the Early Triassic, making it the first marine reptile to become a superpredator.
facts.quote: Thalattoarchon vivió cuatro millones de años después de la primera aparición de los ictiosaurios en el Triásico Inferior y por lo tanto es el primer reptil marino que se volvió un superdepredador.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon lived eight million years after the Permian-Triassic mass extinction, preceding the first appearance of terrestrial superpredators after the Carnian Pluvial Event in the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Vivió ocho millones de años después de la extinción masiva del Pérmico-Triásico, antecediendo la primera aparición de superdepredadores en tierra tras la extinción en masa en la época del Carniense en el Triásico Superior.

facts.statement: The existence of Thalattoarchon suggests that marine ecosystems recovered faster than terrestrial ones after the Permian-Triassic mass extinction.
facts.quote: De esta manera, la existencia de Thalattoarchon sugiere que los ecosistemas marinos se recuperaron más rápido que los terrestres tras dicha extinción.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon is a large ichthyosaur estimated to measure more than 8 meters in length.
facts.quote: Thalattoarchon es un ictiosaurio de gran tamaño que mediría más de 8 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon is diagnosed by a unique feature among ichthyosaurs: large, thin teeth with two cutting edges and smooth dental crowns.
facts.quote: Thalattoarchon ha sido diagnosticado por una característica que es única entre los ictiosaurios: grandes dientes delgados que poseen dos bordes cortantes y poseen coronas dentales lisas.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon resembles the Middle Triassic ichthyosaur Cymbospondylus but differs by having a head nearly twice as large relative to body size.
facts.quote: Thalattoarchon es muy similar en apariencia a Cymbospondylus, otro gran ictiosaurio del Triásico Medio, pero difiere en tener una cabeza que es cerca del doble de grande que la de Cymbospondylus en relación con el tamaño del cuerpo.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon belongs to the parent group Merriamosauria.

facts.statement: Thalattoarchon is classified in the class Reptilia.
